subject: physics_2
question_text: What are the properties of a neutron?

verification.note: The 1+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: neutron rest mass 1.675 × 10⁻²⁷ kg against the proton mass 1.673 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, so "nearly equal to the proton" is right. Free-neutron mean life is about 880 s, close to the book's 1000 s, and the decay ₀n¹ → ₁H¹ + ₋₁e⁰ + antineutrino balances: A 1 = 1 + 0, Z 0 = 1 − 1. Neutron diffraction by crystals is standard and confirms the wave nature.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Charge and mass
lines: A neutron is an uncharged particle.
Its mass is nearly equal to the mass of a
Being neutral, it is not deflected by electric
steps.margin_note: First mark. Charge zero, proton-like mass, no deflection in fields.
steps.why: Every other property in this answer follows from the zero charge, so it belongs in the first line.
common_mistakes: Giving the neutron a small negative charge. It is exactly neutral.
Saying the mass equals the electron mass.

recall.must_convey: That a neutron is uncharged, has mass nearly equal to the proton mass, and is not deflected by electric or magnetic fields.
accept: mass nearly equal to the proton
not deflected by electric and magnetic fields

steps.memory_tip: Neutral and heavy: that pair explains the rest of the list.

steps.label: Penetration and ionization
steps.mark_note: High penetrating power, very low ionizing power
lines: A neutron has very high penetrating power and
It passes through matter without pulling
electrons out of atoms, and loses energy only
when it collides with a nucleus.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The two powers move in opposite directions: penetration high, ionization low.
steps.why: A charged particle is stopped quickly because it ionizes every atom it passes; with no charge the neutron does neither, so it travels far.
common_mistakes: Saying the ionizing power is high. It is very low.
Saying neutrons are stopped by thin lead. They are highly penetrating.

recall.must_convey: That a neutron has very high penetrating power and very low ionizing power, losing energy by collisions with nuclei.
accept: loses energy by collision with nuclei
reject: it decays into a proton and an electron

steps.memory_tip: No ionization on the way in means nothing slows it — high penetration.

steps.label: Stability and decay
steps.mark_note: Stable inside the nucleus, decays when free
lines: Inside a nucleus a neutron is stable.
A free neutron is unstable: in about 1000 s it
decays into a proton, an electron and an
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The contrast between bound and free, plus the decay equation.
steps.why: The equation balances: mass numbers 1 = 1 + 0 and charge numbers 0 = 1 − 1. Inside a nucleus this decay is blocked because there is no free energy level for the extra proton, so bound neutrons last indefinitely.
common_mistakes: Writing a neutrino instead of an antineutrino.
Saying a neutron is unstable everywhere. It is stable inside the nucleus.

recall.must_convey: That a neutron is stable inside the nucleus but a free neutron decays in about 1000 seconds into a proton, an electron and an antineutrino.
accept: free neutron decays into a proton electron and antineutrino

steps.memory_tip: Bound neutron: safe. Free neutron: about a quarter of an hour.

steps.label: Slowing down and diffraction
steps.mark_note: Slowed by light nuclei; diffracted by crystals
lines: Fast neutrons are slowed down when they pass
through heavy water, paraffin wax or graphite,
Neutrons are also diffracted by crystals, which

lines.text: Neutral · penetrates · slowed by light nuclei

steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Name one slowing material and the crystal diffraction.
steps.why: A neutron gives up most energy in a head-on collision with a nucleus of nearly its own mass, which is why hydrogen-rich materials are the best moderators.
common_mistakes: Naming lead as a moderator. Heavy nuclei barely slow a neutron.
Omitting diffraction. It is the property that shows the neutron behaves as a wave.

recall.must_convey: That fast neutrons are slowed by heavy water, paraffin wax or graphite, and that neutrons are diffracted by crystals.
accept: slowed down by heavy water and graphite

steps.memory_tip: Light nuclei brake a neutron best, because equal masses trade the most energy.

insider_note: Four marks, so group the properties into four: charge and mass, penetration, stability, and behaviour in matter. A loose list of eight lines earns no more.
